title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE EMPTY STOOL
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bev Kowalczyk, sixty-one, who weighs grain trucks at an elevator in Great Falls, Montana.
For forty years, Bev drummed on everything. The steering wheel. The scale desk. Her husband's head.
She had never touched a real drum.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE GARAGE BAND
segments.quote: I am always doing what I can't do yet in order to learn how to do it.
segments.author: Vincent van Gogh
lines: Her neighbor Ray, seventy, played bass in a garage band called the Prairie Dogs.
Their drummer moved to Arizona. The stool sat empty.
Bev said, I can't play. Ray handed her a mug with a line from the painter Vincent van Gogh:
I am always doing what I can't do yet in order to learn how to do it.
That Saturday, she bought a used drum set for two hundred dollars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE TEACHER
segments.quote: Time is a great teacher, but unfortunately it kills all its pupils.
segments.author: Hector Berlioz
lines: At her first practice, Bev was lost by the second song.
She said, give me time, I'll figure it out.
Ray laughed and quoted the French composer Hector Berlioz:
Time is a great teacher, but unfortunately it kills all its pupils.
So Bev skipped time and got a real teacher, Tyler, twenty-two, from the music store.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TOO MANY DRUMS
segments.quote: Making the simple complicated is commonplace; making the complicated simple, awesomely simple, that's creativity.
segments.author: Charles Mingus
lines: Now Bev hit every drum in every song, like a raccoon in a pots and pans cupboard.
Tyler wrote a line from jazz bass player Charles Mingus on her practice pad:
Making the simple complicated is commonplace; making the complicated simple, awesomely simple, that's creativity.
So Bev played just three things. Kick, snare, one cymbal. The whole band locked in.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SCALE HOUSE
segments.quote: The formula for success is simple: practice and concentration, then more practice and more concentration.
segments.author: Babe Didrikson Zaharias
lines: The Prairie Dogs booked the harvest dance at the Elks Lodge. Six weeks away.
Bev taped a card by her scale from the great athlete Babe Didrikson Zaharias:
The formula for success is simple: practice and concentration, then more practice and more concentration.
Every lunch break, she drummed pencils on the scale desk. The truckers started tapping along.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE WRONG CRASH
segments.quote: The piano ain't got no wrong notes.
segments.author: Thelonious Monk
lines: Dance night. Two hundred people. Bev's hands shook.
In the first song, she smashed the cymbal at the wrong moment. Loud.
Then she heard Tyler's favorite line, from jazz piano man Thelonious Monk:
The piano ain't got no wrong notes.
So she crashed it again, on purpose, every chorus. Ray grinned. The crowd hit the dance floor.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE STOOL IS HERS
segments.quote: Shared joy is a double joy; shared sorrow is half a sorrow.
segments.author: Swedish proverb
lines: After the last song, Ray's wife Ingrid hugged Bev and said an old Swedish proverb:
Shared joy is a double joy; shared sorrow is half a sorrow.
The truckers were there. Her husband was there. Even Tyler danced.
Ray painted Bev's name on the drum stool. Now the Prairie Dogs play the Elks every month.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start anyway. Get help. Keep it simple. Practice. Own your mistakes. Share the joy.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start before you're ready. Get a teacher. Keep it simple. Practice. Own your mistakes. Share the joy.
I tried the drums once. My neighbors bought me a harmonica. A small one.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
